Finite-difference Jacobian of a vector-valued function

Source: R/06-ae_solver.R
fd_jacobian.Rd

Column j is a central difference with step eps * max(abs(x[j]), 1). With finite lower or upper, no evaluation point leaves the bounds: where one side of a central step would, the difference is one-sided with the same step (forward, or backward when only the lower side fits). When neither side fits, the larger feasible one-sided step is used, max(upper - x, x - lower), and a coordinate with no room at all gives a zero column. Inside the bounds the result is exactly the unbounded one. The "forward" method steps up when that stays inside the bounds and down otherwise.

Usage

fd_jacobian(
  fn,
  x,
  ...,
  eps = 1e-06,
  method = c("central", "forward"),
  check = TRUE,
  lower = -Inf,
  upper = Inf,
  lazy_f0 = FALSE
)

Arguments

fn

A function of a numeric vector returning a numeric vector.

x

The point at which to differentiate, a numeric vector.

...

Further arguments passed to fn.

eps

Relative step size.

method

"central" or "forward" differences.

check

Whether to check that fn returns numeric vectors.

lower, upper

Inclusive bounds of the evaluation points, recycled to the length of x.

lazy_f0

If TRUE, fn(x) is evaluated (and checked as usual) only when a coordinate needs a one-sided or room step; the result is identical. An invalid fn(x) is then detected only when it is used.
